<!-- pr-reviewer: b0ea3433e8f28562dc02f7a6deff13c3cbb56492 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** No blockers.

This is a SAFETY-tier review: the PR changes the stock simulation (the cut layers of `SdfField`).

### What is good

- All writes to the three cut layers go through `layer_brick_mut` (`Arc::make_mut`). The `Arc` type makes a write through a shared brick impossible without this call. I searched the merged tree: there is no other write path to `cuts`, `cut_ups` or `cut_downs`.
- The read-first order in `claim_record` and `up_record` writes the same values as before. An absent brick reads NaN, and NaN always takes the write. A NaN value `v` on a present cell takes no write, as before.
- The flipped bake (`field_turn`) makes new allocations, so a turned field shares no brick with a keyframe.
- The keyframe count compares each key with the key before it by pointer identity. The count can only read high. After a thinning, `thin` sums the count again from the keys that stay. I found no case where the count reads low.
- The decision file `docs/decisions/2194-share-keyframe-bricks.md` records the choice and the options that were dropped.
- No golden moved: no `.nc`, `.cl` or `.png` file is in the diff. No UI change.

### Results, merged with main

Built and tested locally, on the PR head `b0ea343` merged with `upstream/main` `5fdbed9` (clean merge).

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 11 steps, 0 failed.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| sim lib | 192 passed |
| sim `play_keys` | 6 passed |
| sim `play_precalc` | 4 passed |
| sim `stock_carry_side_exact` | 13 passed |
| sim `stock_columns` | 3 passed |
| sim `stock_field_cost` | 4 passed |
| sim `stock_sdf` | 9 passed |
| app `stock_field_cost` | 0 passed, 1 ignored (heavy) |
| app `stock_play_precalc` | 9 passed, 1 ignored (heavy) |

Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`, release, `--ignored`): all 220 steps of the plan ran. 0 failed. The three known-fail tests (#1950 two times, and `pocket3d_hsm`) are red as expected. The run was in two parts, because a background limit stopped the first part during step 146:

- Part 1: steps 1 to 145, all `ok` (motion heavy lanes and app heavy lanes up to `rotary_field_parity`).
- Part 2: steps 146 to 220 with `--only`, 75 steps, 0 failed, wall 64.2 min. This includes `app heavy: rotary_field_parity` (707 s), `stock_engine_agreement`, `stock_field_cost`, `stock_play_precalc` (with `precalc_reading_on_the_dense_face`), `verify` and the `stock_source_*` lanes.

This completes the "Not exercised" item of the PR body about the heavy lanes.

Extra suites run: none apply. The diff does not change `testdata/` or a fixture directory, and it does not touch import code.

### Mutations (SAFETY tier)

Each mutation was applied in the review worktree, run, and then restored.

1. `claim_record` takes the writable slot before the read (`let cur = *self.cut_mut(key);`): `the_keyframes_share_the_bricks_that_no_move_changed` is red, `16358624 bytes held; whole copies cost 45301760`. These are the same numbers as the PR body.
2. `Keyframes::offer` counts `value.key_bytes()`: `a_keyframe_costs_what_the_one_before_does_not_share` is red (`crates/sim/tests/play_keys.rs:88`).
3. `layer_brick_mut` writes through the shared pointer (no copy-on-write): three tests are red.
   - `a_clone_shares_its_cut_bricks_and_a_write_copies_first`: "a shared brick is copied before the write".
   - `the_keyframes_share_the_bricks_that_no_move_changed` (the replay check).
   - The old test `the_precalculated_stock_is_the_live_cut_at_every_position`.

After the restore, the tree was equal to the trial merge again.

### Law check (upstream `AGENTS.md`)

- Prime Directive: no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in non-test code. The byte counts use saturating operations.
- Code shape: all touched source files are below 400 lines (`field.rs` 367, `field_batch.rs` 388).
- Tests are in the lowest crate that provides what they import. The gate map of `crates/sim/tests/play_keys.rs` now names `camcraft_sim::stock_sim::field`.
- No new dependency between our crates. No process file. No `PROCESS_VERSION` edit.
- The commit subject is conventional (`perf(sim): ...`). The body ends with `Fixes #2194`. The PR body has a `Changelog:` line and ends with `Fixes #2194`.

### Notes (not blocking)

- `CostLedger` is still copied whole by each keyframe, and the store does not count it. This is as before, and the PR body and the decision say so.
- A cell write that changes a value now does two map lookups (the read, then `layer_brick_mut`). The dense face reading is faster in total, so this cost is small.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: b0ea3433e8f28562dc02f7a6deff13c3cbb56492 -->
Read-only second review (Opus). Not built here.

Verdict: Ready to merge.

Blockers: none.

### What I read

The full diff of `origin/main...b0ea3433e`: `crates/sim/src/play_keys.rs`, `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field.rs`, `field_batch.rs`, `field_ray.rs`, `field_turn.rs`, `crates/sim/tests/play_keys.rs`, `crates/app/tests/stock_play_precalc.rs` and `docs/decisions/2194-share-keyframe-bricks.md`.

### Copy-on-write correctness

- The three cut layers are now `HashMap<[i32; 3], Arc<[f64; BRICK3]>>`. Write access to the cell values through an `Arc` is possible only with `Arc::make_mut` or `Arc::get_mut`. I searched `crates/sim/src/stock_sim` on the PR head. There is no `Arc::get_mut`, no `unsafe` and no interior mutability on the bricks. The only write paths are `cut_mut` (from `claim_record`) and `up_record`. The two go through `layer_brick_mut`. Thus the compiler makes sure that a write never reaches a brick that a keyframe shares. A keyframe stays an exact prefix of the program.
- `cut_downs` gets values only from the flip bake in `field_turn`. That bake makes new allocations (`Axes::cut_layer`) and shares no brick. This is correct.
- `claim_record` and `up_record` now read first. I compared the old and the new branch conditions. An absent brick reads NaN, and NaN always takes the write. Thus the set of bricks, the written values, the `full` ledger and the `dirty` set are the same as before. Only a visit that changes no cell does not copy a brick now.
- Value semantics of `SdfField` and `Stock` do not change. Each clone (keyframe, restore, live stock, post gate) sees the same values as a deep copy. Thus a gouge, collision or rest-material reading from a keyframe is the same as before.

### Equality pins

- `a_clone_shares_its_cut_bricks_and_a_write_copies_first` compares a field cut over shared bricks with a field cut with no clone, bit for bit. It also checks that the clone does not change after a write into a shared brick.
- `the_keyframes_share_the_bricks_that_no_move_changed` compares the replay with the live cut at six positions, forward and backward, bit for bit. It also asserts that the running count equals the audit.
- The old pin `the_precalculated_stock_is_the_live_cut_at_every_position` is not changed. The first review shows that it goes red when `layer_brick_mut` writes through the shared pointer.
- No test was removed or made weaker. The `same` helper in `field_turn` tests is now generic over the brick pointer type. It still compares bits.

### Memory and threads

- The bricks are plain arrays in an `Arc`. A reference cycle is not possible. A brick is freed when the last keyframe or field that holds it is dropped. Delete of the operation drops the store as before.
- `Arc<[f64; 512]>` is `Send` and `Sync`. `Arc::make_mut` is safe when the worker thread and the UI thread hold clones.
- The budget count is never low for the bricks. Each brick allocation is counted at the first keyframe that holds it, because a brick that is replaced never comes back to a later keyframe. After a live seek, equal bricks in new allocations count again, which is what the memory holds. After a thinning, `held_bytes` sums again.

### Law check

- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside tests. The byte math uses saturating operations. The index math (`brick_of`, `in_brick`) did not change.
- All touched files are below 400 lines (`field.rs` 367, `field_batch.rs` 388, `play_keys.rs` 204).
- Test placement is correct. The sim tests import only `camcraft_sim`. The app test uses `FieldPlay` from `camcraft-app`. The gate map line names the new covered module.
- No new dependency between our crates. No process file.
- The decision file uses the format of `docs/decisions/README.md`.
- The PR body has a `Changelog:` line and ends with `Fixes #2194`. The commit body ends with `Fixes #2194`.

### Notes (not blocking)

- `cut_bytes_after` and `KeyCost::key_bytes_after` say "never under the truth". This is true for the bricks. The map entry cost uses `len * size_of::<entry>()`. The real hash map has more buckets than entries and one control byte for each bucket. Thus the map part can read low. Before this PR the map was not counted at all, so this is not a regression. A future change can use `capacity()` in place of `len()` if the count must be strict.
- `CostLedger` is still copied whole by each keyframe and is not counted. This is as before, and the decision file says so.
- `precalc_reading_on_the_dense_face` now runs the dense precalculation two times. It is in the heavy lane, so the cost is only at a cut.
